newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RAUL INSPIRES REAL TO MADRID DERBY SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-RAUL INSPIRES REAL TO MADRID DERBY SUCCESS.

text.p: Real Madrid took a giant leap towards their 27th Spanish league title on Saturday when teenage striker Raul Gonzalez led them to a 4-1 victory over neighbours Atletico.

Raul scored twice against his old side as Real came from behind to swamp their neighbours in a frantic last ten minutes. The result leaves Real six points clear of second-placed Barcelona, who face Real Betis on Sunday, and 11 ahead of reigning champions Atletico.
Raul, who joined Real on a free transfer after Atletico's junior teams were scrapped as a cost-cutting measure, saved the blushes of teammate Predrag Mijatovic, who had a nightmare debut derby.

The Montenegrin had squandered several clear chances as Real opened strongly. Mijatovic was twice denied by brave work from Jose Molina, but left the Atletico keeper stranded with his best effort, a long-distance lob in the 15th minute that floated just over the bar.
Atletico went ahead against the run of play in the 32nd minute when Kiko Narvaez rose to head home a cross by Veljko Paunovic in only Atletico's third attempt on goal.
Radomir Antic's side could have increased their lead before the interval but had to settle for a 1-0 half-time score.
Raul then kept his cool to side-foot home the equaliser just after the break, and was instrumental in his side's resurgence.

Real kept up the pressure despite having Mijatovic sent off for insulting a linesman in the 68th minute, and took the lead eight minutes from time when Raul beat several players to score a superb individual effort from an impossibly tight angle.

Dutch international Clarence Seedorf capitalised on a mistake at the back to make it three shortly afterwards with his first goal for Real, and substitute Victor Sanchez rifled home a shot off the underside of the crossbar on the final whistle to seal the 4-1 win.
There was unanimous praise for Raul afterwards.
"It's difficult to explain how we lost like that. Raul was decisive," Atletico coach Radomir Antic said.

Antic's counterpart, Real manager Fabio Capello, was clearly delighted with his team. "Winning with ten men, in Atletico's ground ...anyone expecting a final part like that would have been mad," he said.

Atletico - 1-Jose Molina, 3-Toni Munoz, 6-Santi Denia, 9-Juan Eduardo Esnaider (17-Juan Carlos Gomez, 65), 10-Milinko Pantic, 19-Kiko Narvaez (8-Juan Vizcaino, 76), 20-Delfi Geli, 21-Jose Luis Caminero, 23-Daniel Prodan (5-Juan Lopez, 70), 24-Radek Bejbl, 27-Veljko Paunovic.

Real - 1-Bodo Illgner, 3-Roberto Carlos, 4-Fernando Hierro, 6-Fernando Redondo, 7-Raul Gonzalez, 8-Predrag Mijatovic (sent off 68), 9-Davor Suker (19-Victor Sanchez 80), 10-Clarence Seedorf, 11-Emilio Amavisca, 17-Christian Panucci, 18-Rafael Alkorta.
